attrs.label: Health content has to be right, every time
attrs.html:
Health content has to be right, every time

People make decisions about their health from what they read. Pick a challenge to see how we handle it.

The challengeSearch engines hold health content to the highest standard. One wrong statement can harm a patient, and your reputation.

Our approach

Make every piece accurate, sourced and reviewed by a named clinician.

People make decisions about their health from what they read. Search engines know that, and so do patients, so health content is held to the highest standard.

In practice

  • Writers with health backgrounds, matched to your specialty
  • Current guidance and research cited on the page
  • A named clinician reviews and signs each piece
  • Review dates, so advice never goes stale

Why it matters

Accurate, reviewed content is what ranks, and what patients trust enough to act on.

Methods we use

  1. 1Health specialist writers

    Writers with medical, nursing, pharmacy and health tech backgrounds.

  2. 2Current clinical sources

    Guidance and research, cited on the page.

  3. 3Named clinical review

    A qualified clinician checks and signs each piece.

  4. 4Review dates

    Every piece rechecked when guidance changes.

What you get

  • Reviewed content
  • Source lists
  • A review schedule

The challengeBig health sites and government pages rank first for almost every condition.

Our approach

Win the treatment and local questions they don’t answer.

You won’t outrank a national health site for “cataract symptoms”. But they don’t answer what it costs at your clinic, how long recovery takes with your team, or who your surgeon is.

In practice

  • Research into the treatment questions patients ask before booking
  • A page for each clinic and treatment
  • Your clinicians’ experience in every guide
  • Answers structured for AI tools and featured results

Why it matters

Treatment and local questions bring in patients who are close to booking.

Methods we use

  1. 1Treatment questions

    Cost, recovery and suitability, answered for your clinic.

  2. 2Local pages

    A page for each clinic and the treatments it offers.

  3. 3Your clinicians’ view

    Experience and advice big sites can’t offer.

  4. 4Answers AI can quote

    Clear, structured answers for AI tools and featured results.

What you get

  • A search gap map
  • Treatment pages
  • Local pages

The challengeSelf-pay and planned treatments are big decisions. Patients read, worry and compare for weeks before they book.

Our approach

Answer every worry, in the order patients have them.

A patient considering surgery or fertility treatment doesn’t book after one visit. They come back many times, with a new worry each time.

In practice

  • We find real worries from front desk calls and reviews
  • A guide for each worry, in the order patients have them
  • Clear cost pages with payment options
  • Emails that send the next guide at the right time

Why it matters

When every worry has an answer, patients book sooner, and with your clinic.

Methods we use

  1. 1Worry mapping

    We listen to front desk calls and read reviews to find real worries.

  2. 2What-to-expect guides

    Each step of treatment, day by day.

  3. 3Clear cost pages

    What it costs and what’s included, with payment options.

  4. 4Emails over weeks

    A guide by email for each stage of the decision.

What you get

  • Decision guides
  • Cost pages
  • Patient emails

The challengeHealth advertising, patient privacy and professional rules limit claims, results and patient stories.

Our approach

Check every piece against the rules for your market, before it reaches review.

What you can say about treatments, results and patients is limited by advertising, privacy and professional rules. Getting it wrong means complaints, or content coming down.

In practice

  • A claims checklist for your market and specialty
  • Written consent for every story, photo and quote
  • Patient details changed or removed where needed
  • A record of who reviewed each piece, and when

Why it matters

Content that follows the rules stays up, and keeps bringing in patients.

Methods we use

  1. 1A claims checklist

    What you can and can’t say about treatments and results.

  2. 2A consent process

    Written consent for every story, photo and quote.

  3. 3Privacy-safe stories

    Details changed or removed where needed.

  4. 4Records for regulators

    Who reviewed what, and when.

What you get

  • A claims checklist
  • Consent forms
  • Review records

The challengeYour specialists know the most, but their diaries are full.

Our approach

Short interviews and quick reviews that fit around clinics.

Your clinicians are the experts patients want to hear from, and the people with the least free time. So we keep their part short.

In practice

  • A 20-minute interview gives us enough for a full guide
  • Drafts written in their voice
  • Clean drafts with questions marked, for a quick review
  • Interviews planned around clinic and theatre days

Why it matters

Your clinicians’ knowledge is what makes your content different. We make it easy to share.

Methods we use

  1. 120-minute interviews

    We ask the questions; they talk.

  2. 2Drafts in their voice

    Written so it sounds like them, not like marketing.

  3. 3One-round reviews

    Clean drafts with the questions marked, so reviews are quick.

  4. 4A clinic-friendly calendar

    Interviews booked around theatre lists and clinics.

What you get

  • Clinician interviews
  • Ready-to-review drafts
  • A content calendar

The challengeGPs, opticians and physios send patients to clinics they trust. Most clinic sites say nothing to them.

Our approach

Give referrers the clinical detail they need to refer with confidence.

Many patients arrive through a referral. Referrers choose clinics they know and trust, and they read very different content from patients.

In practice

  • Clear referral criteria for each treatment
  • Short clinical updates from your specialists
  • Anonymised case summaries
  • Evening talks written up as articles and emails

Why it matters

A referrer who trusts you can send patients for years.

Methods we use

  1. 1Referral criteria pages

    Who to refer, when, and how.

  2. 2Clinical updates

    Short, referenced updates from your specialists.

  3. 3Case summaries

    Anonymised examples of complex cases and outcomes.

  4. 4Events and learning

    Evening talks and learning sessions, written up as content.

What you get

  • A referrer hub
  • Clinical updates
  • Event content

The challengePatients ask AI tools about symptoms and treatments. Those tools quote clear, trusted sources.

Our approach

Be the trusted source AI tools quote.

Patients now ask AI tools “is this normal after surgery?” or “who is it suitable for?”. Those tools quote a few trusted sources. You want to be one of them.

In practice

  • The answer in the first lines of every page
  • A named clinical reviewer on every page
  • Clear headings, lists and markup
  • Monthly checks of which AI tools quote you

Why it matters

AI answers are the new first page of search, and they favour reviewed, well-sourced content.

Methods we use

  1. 1Answer-first pages

    The answer in the first lines, then the detail.

  2. 2Named reviewers

    Clear signs that a clinician stands behind each page.

  3. 3Structured pages

    Headings, lists and markup that AI tools read easily.

  4. 4Citation tracking

    We check which AI tools quote you, and for what.

What you get

  • Answer-first pages
  • Structured markup
  • AI citation reports

attrs.label: Patients and clinicians, two different voices
attrs.html:
Patients and clinicians, two different voices

The same topic needs to be written very differently for a worried patient and a busy specialist. We write for both, and every piece is checked for accuracy before it goes live.

How we keep it accurate

  • Writers with health and medical backgrounds
  • Sources from current clinical guidance, cited on the page
  • Review by a qualified clinician, named on the page
  • Checked against the advertising rules for your market
  • Review dates, so advice never goes stale

Same topic: recovery after cataract surgery

After cataract surgery, most people see more clearly within a few days. Your eye may feel gritty or watery for a week or two. This is normal and usually settles on its own. Use your eye drops as shown, and avoid rubbing your eye.

  • Reading age of 11 to 12
  • No jargon, or jargon explained
  • What to do next, and when to call
  • Reviewed by a clinician

Same topic: recovery after cataract surgery

Post-operative visual recovery after phacoemulsification is typically rapid, with most patients achieving functional acuity within the first week. Transient ocular surface symptoms are common and generally self-limiting with standard topical therapy.

  • Clinical terminology
  • Referenced to current guidance
  • Outcome data where available
  • Reviewed by a specialist

attrs.title: Healthcare content marketing questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is healthcare content marketing?
items.answer: It’s creating accurate, useful content, such as patient guides, treatment pages and articles for clinicians, that helps people make health decisions and choose your clinic or product.

items.question: Who reviews the content?
items.answer: Every piece is reviewed by a qualified clinician: one of yours, or a reviewer we provide with the right specialty. Their name and review date appear on the page.

items.question: Do you write for healthcare professionals as well as patients?
items.answer: Yes. We write separately for patients and for clinicians, with different language, depth and sources.

items.question: How much does healthcare content marketing cost?
items.answer: Every programme is a fixed monthly price, based on how much content you need and the review involved. We quote after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How do you handle patient stories?
items.answer: Only with written consent, and within the advertising and privacy rules for your market.

items.question: Do you use AI to write content?
items.answer: No. Health content needs accuracy and accountability, so every piece is written and checked by people.
